boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Redlands-campus places with documented ways students gather, learn, make, move, or take a quiet break.

cards.title: Set up a research-and-study session
cards.subtitle: Library study spaces and research support
cards.notes: Choose a study space, then use the library’s research consultations or lending services when a project needs more than a laptop session.
cards.short_summary: A campus library for study space, borrowing, and individualized research help.
cards.evidence_claim: Armacost Library provides study spaces, book lending, interlibrary loans, and personalized research consultations.
cards.access_notes: Campus library; consult the library for current access details.

cards.title: Plan a low-key evening with campus programming
cards.subtitle: Student-life hub beside Irvine Commons
cards.notes: Check student-life programming for an activity here; orientation materials describe Hunsaker After Dark with games, music, and social activities.
cards.short_summary: A central student-life setting used for organized social programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The 2025 orientation guide describes Hunsaker After Dark as games, music, and activities for students to unwind and socialize.
cards.source_title: New Student Orientation Guidebook | University of Redlands
cards.access_notes: Programming and access vary by event.

cards.title: Use an orientation-day meeting point
cards.subtitle: Main-campus event and meeting venue
cards.notes: Look for scheduled orientation sessions, workshops, or campus events here; the university places spring orientation in the Orton Center.
cards.short_summary: A named venue used for new-student orientation and other campus gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Redlands states that spring orientation takes place in the Orton Center.
cards.source_title: New Student Experience | University of Redlands
cards.access_notes: Event attendance and room access depend on the scheduled program.

cards.title: Find a public campus gathering on the lawn
cards.subtitle: Central outdoor event space
cards.notes: Watch the campus calendar for community events on the Quad, including the Living on Common Ground Multicultural Festival and student programming.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor campus setting for cultural festivals, dinners, and other shared events.
cards.evidence_claim: The university’s 2026 Multicultural Festival is scheduled on the University Quad and invites students, families, and community members.
cards.access_notes: Open-event access varies by calendar listing.

cards.title: Attend a campus welcome or performance
cards.subtitle: Historic chapel and large-event venue
cards.notes: Check the events calendar for a scheduled gathering or performance; orientation programming uses the chapel for the University Convocation.
cards.short_summary: A large campus venue used for convocation, speaking events, and performances.
cards.evidence_claim: The 2025 orientation guide schedules the University of Redlands Convocation in Memorial Chapel.
cards.source_title: New Student Orientation Guidebook 2025 | University of Redlands
cards.access_notes: Event attendance and chapel access depend on the scheduled program.

cards.title: Take a calm garden break or volunteer
cards.subtitle: Campus community garden
cards.notes: Use the garden as a quiet outdoor reset, or ask Community Service Learning about gardening work and volunteer opportunities connected to it.
cards.short_summary: A student-developed community garden that also supports gardening work.
cards.evidence_claim: The university identifies LaFourcade Community Garden as student-developed and says students can work there as gardeners.
cards.access_notes: Garden work opportunities are coordinated through Community Service Learning.

cards.title: Learn through hands-on garden work
cards.subtitle: Campus farm near the athletic fields
cards.notes: Ask Community Service Learning about volunteer or work-study options; students maintain crop growth and support campus and local food distribution.
cards.short_summary: A student-maintained farm tied to sustainability work and food distribution.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Redlands says students work at S.U.R.F. daily to maintain crops, which go to campus food service or local food distribution programs.
cards.access_notes: Work and volunteer participation should be arranged through Community Service Learning.

cards.title: Walk a reflective campus loop
cards.subtitle: Located by Memorial Chapel
cards.notes: Use the labyrinth for a short, quiet reset between commitments; the university lists walking it among campus options for finding calm.
cards.short_summary: A named reflective outdoor feature next to Memorial Chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: The university’s LiveWell guidance recommends walking the Labyrinth, located by Memorial Chapel, as a way to find calm on campus.
cards.access_notes: Use respectfully and yield to any scheduled campus activity nearby.

cards.title: Recognize the graduation-stage landmark
cards.subtitle: Outdoor Greek Theatre on the Redlands campus
cards.notes: Spot this outdoor theatre on a campus walk, then check university event listings before planning to attend a ceremony or other programmed gathering.
cards.short_summary: A named campus theatre associated with graduates crossing the stage.
cards.evidence_claim: The University of Redlands alumni office identifies Alumni Greek Theatre as the place where alumni crossed the stage.
cards.access_notes: Use and entry depend on scheduled ceremonies or events.

cards.title: Cheer a campus aquatic event
cards.subtitle: Aquatic center on the north side of campus
cards.notes: Check athletics and event schedules for a meet or special event; Homecoming programming has used the pool for the student-and-alumni Regatta Boat Race.
cards.short_summary: A named aquatic venue used for water-sport competition and special event programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The university’s Homecoming schedule listed the Redlands Regatta Boat Race at Thompson Aquatic Center, with students and alumni racing handmade boats.
cards.access_notes: Pool and event access depend on athletics or event scheduling.
